name: PCV Valve
summary: Owner decision: category retained. Evidence says the N52 (later production) has no standalone, user-replaceable PCV valve: crankcase ventilation (oil separation/pressure regulation, with a rubber diaphragm per one forum source) is integrated in the plastic valve cover, sold as a complete cover kit, OE 11127552281 (Turner x2, Febi 194977 per Turner, URO/Turner, bavmods cross-reference). Early-production N52 (2006 and some 2007) had a separate separator under the intake manifold, reported only by one retailer. Therefore the guide should be an inspect/diagnose/serviceability guide (symptoms, hose and cap checks, vent hose 11157559528, when to replace the whole valve cover) and must NOT contain a standalone valve procedure. A full valve-cover replacement procedure (step order, torque, sequence, seals, required disassembly such as Valvetronic motor, throttle body seal part number) was NOT found and is MISSING; the only torque (7 Nm + 90 degrees, single-use aluminum bolts) is single-source and uncertain.
variantDependencies: Early N52 (2006 and some 2007 production): replaceable oil separator under the intake manifold (kit 11617531423 etc. per one Turner page). A 2010 build is expected to be the later integrated design, but the build date is UNCONFIRMED.
N51B30 SULEV: URO page says the same plastic valve cover fits N51 SULEV and N52; N51 CCV differences otherwise unresearched.
N52K (black-top) cover redesign mentioned by one forum poster as different/harder to service; unverified and may not apply to a 2010 US 328i.
xDrive vs RWD and manual vs auto: no effect found.

steps.title: Understand what is serviceable
steps.instruction: The N52 crankcase ventilation oil separator and pressure regulator are built into the plastic valve cover; no standalone PCV valve is sold. The serviceable items are the external vent hoses and the complete valve cover. Do not attempt to remove or replace a standalone valve.
steps.status: VERIFIED (3 independent sources: Turner/URO, bavmods, xoutpost forum)

steps.title: Check build era
steps.instruction: Confirm production date: early N52 (2006, some 2007) had a separate separator under the intake manifold; later engines do not.

steps.title: Observe symptoms
steps.instruction: Possible signs: rough idle, whistling or vacuum leak, higher oil consumption, sooty tailpipe, oil in the intake path, CEL; oil at throttle body is an easier check than the separator itself.

steps.title: Inspect hoses and breather connection
steps.instruction: With engine cold and cover off, check CCV hoses for brittleness, cracks or oil seepage; the nipple on the diaphragm housing is described as an atmospheric vent, not for a hose (single forum source).

steps.title: Optional blow-through test
steps.instruction: One poster suggests disconnecting the CCV pipes and blowing through to check the path to the sump; not verified for E90 N52.
warnings: Do not blow into coolant or oil vapor lines by mouth; avoid ingesting oil mist.

steps.title: Decide: replace valve cover
steps.instruction: If the diaphragm/passages are suspected failed or clogged, the fix described by multiple sources is the whole valve cover (OE 11127552281) plus vent hose 11157559528; cleaning is described as nearly impossible.

steps.title: Valve cover replacement procedure
steps.instruction: Ordered removal/installation steps, required disassembly (for example Valvetronic motor for the middle bolt, throttle body seal), torque and sequence were NOT found in usable form.
warnings: Aluminum bolts are reported single-use; reusing them or overtightening can strip or break them.

safety: Engine must be cold before removing the cover or hoses.
Oil leaks onto hot exhaust parts can cause smoke or fire; clean spills fully.
Do not publish torque values for valve cover bolts without a BMW source; forum values are single-source.
Use only OE or quality cover assemblies; one forum describes problems with no-name covers (single source).
Do not fabricate or imply a standalone PCV valve procedure.
